sense: have the benefit of: good health, a right

terms.gloss: have, enjoy (health, good weather, a friendship, an office)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative
evidence: Caes. BC 3.49.2: ūtī autem ipsōs valētūdine nōn bonā
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to experience, undergo, receive, enjoy”: valētūdine bonā ūtī, to enjoy good health (Traupman 61); amplissimīs honōribus ūtī, to have held the highest offices (Cic. Fl. 45, Lewis & Short). The same verb is “use”.

terms.gloss: enjoy (a good one has: peace, liberty, life)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 131: commoda quibus ūtimur lūcemque quā fruimur (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Mīrum est, nam valētūdine bonā ūteris.
phrases.english: That’s strange, since you enjoy good health.

phrases.latin: suum cuique per mē ūtī atque fruī licet
phrases.english: as far as I am concerned, everyone may have and enjoy what is his

sources: Lewis & Short: utor · Lewis & Short: fruor
